plugins.name: @kinetographdev/hexed
plugins.title: Hexed
plugins.description: Rolls a look onto any picture or clip from eleven slots, such as grade, screen, optics and damage. Lock what you like and shuffle the rest.
about: Hexed rolls a look onto a picture or a clip. The look is made of eleven slots: crop, shake, fps, time, mirror, isolate, grade, screen, optics, damage and grunge. Each slot holds one gene (a named effect, such as a sepia print grade or a twelve-frame-a-second stutter), a seed and an amount.

The whole look is a genome: plain JSON with one strand per slot. A genome plays back the same every time, so a look you like can be kept in code or saved as a preset. Roll from a seed, lock the slots you want to keep, and reroll the rest.
Use it when a video needs a grade, glitch, grain, shake or print look, or when you want to reroll and save looks.

componentDocs.name: Hexed
componentDocs.summary: Wraps any children. It fills the composition unless you give a width and height.
props: Rolls a gene for each slot. Default 1.
Slots to hold while the seed changes. A seed, a gene id, or a partial strand per slot.
A saved look. Wins over seed and lock.
A saved look by name from presets/. Wins over seed and lock.
Slots to switch off, for example ["grunge"].
Strength of the whole look, 0 to 1. Default 1.
Strength per slot, 0 to 1, on top of the genome's own.
The order the effect slots run in.
Scans the grunge slot picks from, as { src, kind }.
Global exposure, shadows, highlights, contrast, saturation and temperature (each -100 to 100), hue (degrees), sharpen (0 to 100) and invert.
The picture's size and top-left corner on the canvas, for a picture that does not fill the frame.
componentDocs.after: Other exports: roll(seed, lock?, textures?) returns a genome, describe(genome, off?) names it in one line, genesOf(slot) lists the gene ids a slot accepts, and PRESETS holds the saved genomes. hexedSchema is the zod schema for the props, and genomeSchema is the schema for a genome.

plugins.presetNote: Presets live in presets/*.json. Roll and save one with the plugin’s save-preset tool.

examples.title: Roll a look onto a clip
Lock a slot, switch one off, or use a saved look

studio.panel: A Hexed panel for any prop that uses genomeSchema: one card per slot with a gene list, an amount slider, a lock and the slot’s seed (click to copy), a shuffle per slot, a Shuffle button for the whole look that keeps locked slots, and a preset menu. It follows Studio’s light and dark theme.

tools.name: hexed_roll
tools.text: Rolls a look and returns { seed, genome }. Without a seed it picks one and returns it, so the roll can be repeated. With a genome in from and slot names in locks, the locked slots keep their strands and the rest reroll.

tools.name: hexed_genes
tools.text: Lists the gene ids each slot accepts, with a note on the slot. Takes an optional slot.

tools.name: hexed_presets
tools.text: Returns the saved looks as { name: genome }.

studio.note: The tools are available while Kinetograph’s MCP server is running (kinetograph mcp). Try looks with studio_set_props, then write the settled genome into the code or save it as a preset; do not leave it only in Studio’s live props.
studio.installed: Run `npx kinetograph plugins` to see that a plugin is installed; agents read its skill from there.

plugins.name: @kinetographdev/kinetic-typography
plugins.title: Kinetic Typography
plugins.description: Hand-written captions that write on letter by letter to a voiceover, with key words breaking out in display faces, optionally hung off a tracked subject.
about: HandCaptions writes a voiceover on screen letter by letter. Each word writes itself across its spoken time, every letter in a different handwritten face, so it reads as one restless hand. Key words break out whole in a display face: a fat serif with a doodle beside it, or a heavy italic that streaks in.

The captions can hang off a tracked subject. They sit beside it on the side where they fit, with a reticle on the subject, lines to the text and off the frame, and a bracket with coordinates on the letter being written. Without a tracked subject they sit centred low.

componentDocs.name: HandCaptions
componentDocs.summary: Writes a list of timed words on screen. Letters glow warm and land with a pink and cyan fringe.
props: { text, from, to } per word, in frames. wordsFrom(stamps, fps, at) makes them from timestamps in seconds.
Words per page. Default 3 a page. A page stays until the next starts, or 12 frames after its last word.
Words that break out, matched without case or punctuation.
(frame) => { x, y } | null: a tracked subject. Without it the captions sit centred low.
Where the text hangs when it should not follow the subject; the lines still run to the subject.
Letter size (default 124 px at 1080 high), colour, glow (a text-shadow, empty for none) and the landing fringe.
The handwritten faces mixed per letter (Caveat, Shadows Into Light, Indie Flower, Gloria Hallelujah, Patrick Hand, Gochi Hand) and the two display faces (Abril Fatface, Archivo Black).
The doodle's colour or false; the reticle's label or false; the lines on or off.
The highest the block may reach.
componentDocs.after: wordSpans(words, split, hot) gives when each word is written, to cue a pen sound on plain words and a thump on key words.

examples.title: Captions from word timestamps
Hung off a tracked subject

studio.note: The plugin ships a skill and no Studio panel or agent tools. The skill tells an agent to get word timestamps from an ASR or TTS list rather than place frames by hand, to choose the pages and key words, to track the subject with the VJ plugin’s point tracker, and to render stills on a few word frames to check the block fits.
studio.installed: Run `npx kinetograph plugins` to see that a plugin is installed; agents read its skill from there.

plugins.name: @kinetographdev/paper
plugins.title: Paper
plugins.description: A paper material with creases, scans and grain, and effects made of it: a text match cut over changing pages, and photo cut-outs that fold open.
about: Paper is a paper material (creases, scans, grain) and the effects made of it. MatchCut holds a highlighted keyword still while the page under it changes several times a second, on made-up pages or on your own screenshots. CutOut turns a photo with its background removed into a paper cut-out, and FoldOut unfolds it flap by flap in stop motion.

MatchCut comes with four looks to start from (web, broadsheet, crumpled and clean) and a look object that overrides any of them. With your own screenshots you give a rough box around the word and it snaps to it.
Use it for fast keyword-over-pages edits and paper-craft looks.

componentDocs.name: MatchCut
componentDocs.summary: A keyword holds still, highlighted, while the page under it changes several times a second. It fills its composition.
props: The word or phrase that holds still. Required.
A look by name: web, broadsheet, crumpled or clean.
A partial look that overrides the preset.
Your own pages: { src, hint: [x, y, w, h], exact? }. src is under public/.
A screenshot every nth cut. 1 means screenshots only. Default 3.
Draws the hint (blue) and the snapped box (red) on screenshots.
Frames the push-in runs over. Default the composition's.
componentDocs.after: The look fields are layouts, cutsPerSecond, zoom, keySize, anchorY, blur, smear, falloff, streak, crumple, tint, texture, textureOpacity, grain, highlight and wander. matchCutSchema and matchCutLookSchema are the zod schemas for the props and for look. flicks({ frames, fps, cutsPerSecond }) at the top level of the entry adds a paper flick on every cut.

componentDocs.name: CutOut
componentDocs.summary: A photo with its background already removed (a PNG with alpha) as a paper cut-out.
props: Size and place on the canvas.
How creased, how deep the shadow, how fast the edge redraws, and another take.
The alpha value that counts as inside.

componentDocs.name: FoldOut
componentDocs.summary: A CutOut that unfolds. It takes the CutOut props and adds delay, duration, steps, folds and ball. unfolds({ fps, delay }) adds its sounds.

componentDocs.name: Paper
componentDocs.summary: The paper material the other components are made of. Its props are not described in the plugin’s skill.

presets.name: broadsheet
presets.line: Newspaper layouts (pull quote, italic, kicker, body, display) at ten cuts a second, with a closer push-in.

presets.name: clean
presets.line: Eight cuts a second on near-white paper with no blur, streak, crumple, grain or wander.

presets.name: crumpled
presets.line: The fastest and roughest: twelve cuts a second, heavy smear, streak and crumple, some grain.

presets.name: web
presets.line: Web pages and social posts, ten cuts a second, a strong blur and streak, creased grey paper, a yellow highlight.

plugins.presetNote: The four MatchCut looks are in presets/match-cut/*.json. Picking one in the Studio panel replaces look with that preset’s fields; what it leaves out falls back to MatchCut’s defaults.

examples.title: A match cut on made-up pages
On your own screenshots
examples.code:
<MatchCut
  keyword="Super Bowl"
  screenshots={[{ src: 'shots/a.png', hint: [212, 1180, 388, 64] }]}
  everyNth={1}
  showKeyBox
/>

studio.panel: matchCutLookSchema carries the Paper panel, so Studio mounts it for a look field instead of a generated form. It has preset cards with a drawn swatch, a layout picker with a thumbnail per layout, sliders for keyword size and height, cuts per second, push-in, blur, streak, crumple, grain and wander, colour pickers for the highlight and the paper tint, and a keyword box on the preview you drag to set anchorY and keySize. cutOutLookSchema and foldOutLookSchema carry a sheet view: edge cards and stock cards (white, newsprint, kraft), sliders for creases, shadow, boil and seed, and on the preview a handle to place the picture.
studio.note: The plugin adds no agent tools. Inside Studio, set values with studio_set_props and read the result in the preview, then write the chosen look into the code or a preset. Give the composition look: matchCutLookSchema and leave preset out of its schema, since the preset cards write into look.
studio.installed: Run `npx kinetograph plugins` to see that a plugin is installed; agents read its skill from there.

plugins.name: @kinetographdev/vj
plugins.title: VJ
plugins.description: Screen, tape and sensor looks (CRT, VHS, 1-bit, thermal, depth, pixels) and tracking overlays: boxes on moving blobs and a reticle on one point.
about: VJ adds looks that make a picture seem to come from a screen, a tape or a sensor: a CRT with curved glass, scanlines and a switch-off, a worn VHS tape, a 1-bit dither in two inks, a thermal camera palette, a depth pass, and a magnifier that resolves into red, green and blue subpixels. Each look is a layer effect. Brightness stands in for heat and for depth, so these are looks, not measurements.

It also draws tracking overlays. A blob tracker runs once, offline, over a clip and writes JSON; Blobs then draws boxes, ids, coordinates and links from that JSON on every frame, so a render stays a pure function of the frame. A second tool follows one patch of the picture, and Reticle puts a ticked box on it.

componentDocs.name: Blobs
componentDocs.summary: Draws the tracked blobs over the clip, at the same size.
props: The JSON from the blob tracker.
The composition frame the clip starts on. The track is read by time, so a 24 fps clip in a 30 fps film lines up.
id, xy (centre, 0 to 1), both or none.
nearest, chain (id order), all (pairs within reach of the diagonal) or none.
0 to 1: the share of blobs filled solid in difference blending, inverting the picture under them.
difference keeps the marks readable on white and black alike. Default normal.
Leave out small blobs; keep the biggest few.
color, stroke, fontSize, width, height, id
Styling, size and layer id prefix.
componentDocs.after: blobsAt(track, frame, fps, width, height, from) gives the blobs on a frame, to pin anything else to them.

componentDocs.name: Reticle
componentDocs.summary: A ticked box on one tracked point: <Reticle track label="TRK 01" />. pointAt(track, frame, fps) gives the point itself.

componentDocs.name: crt(o)
componentDocs.summary: A colour tube: curved glass, rounded face, scanlines, aperture grille, misconvergence, breathing exposure, a rolling bar, static and dark corners. Options: cx, cy, hw, hh (the face; default the whole layer), curve, pitch, scan, grille, mask, conv, noise, glass, offx, offy.

componentDocs.name: switchOff(t)
componentDocs.summary: The tube switching off over t from 0 to 1: the picture folds to a line, the line to a dot. Spread it into crt: crt({ ...switchOff(t) }).

componentDocs.name: vhs(o)
componentDocs.summary: A worn tape: line wobble, late smeared colour, a head-switch tear along the bottom, a drifting tracking band, snow and dropouts. Options: jitter, wobble, trackAt (0 to 1, animate it), trackW, track, bleed, delay, sat, snow, drops.

componentDocs.name: oneBit(o)
componentDocs.summary: One bit a pixel: an ordered dither in two inks. Options: size, punch, ink, paper.

componentDocs.name: thermal(o)
componentDocs.summary: A thermal camera's palette on the picture's brightness, a little soft. Options: palette (IRON, RAINBOW or your own stops), soft.

componentDocs.name: depthLook(o)
componentDocs.summary: A depth pass: smooth grey, near is white. Options: soft, punch.

componentDocs.name: pixels(o)
componentDocs.summary: A magnifier: blocks, then red, green and blue subpixel stripes as zoom grows. Options: zoom, cx, cy.

examples.title: A look and tracked boxes over a clip
Track once, offline, then draw
examples.code:
# finds what moved since the last frame; --debug writes every 10th frame with its boxes
node plugins/vj/tools/blobs.mjs --in public/clip.mp4 --out track/clip-blobs.json --debug out/blobs

# follows one patch (x, y, w, h on the first frame)
node plugins/vj/tools/track.mjs --in public/clip.mp4 --box 900,300,120,120 --out track/clip-point.json

studio.panel: Two schemas carry the plugin’s panel. vjLookSchema gives a card per look (none, CRT, VHS, 1-bit, thermal, depth, pixels) and the chosen look’s sliders and colours; each look keeps its own settings when you switch, and on the preview the CRT’s tube face is a box to drag and resize and the magnifier’s centre a cross to drag. blobStyleSchema gives the marks: box, label, links and blend as segmented choices, and sliders for most blobs, smallest, link reach, inverted share, line width, label size and colour. lookEffects(look) turns the look into layer effects, and the marks spread into Blobs.
studio.note: The panel only sets props. Tracking stays a command, because a browser panel cannot run ffmpeg. The plugin adds no agent tools; the skill walks an agent through running the tracker, opening two or three of the debug images, tuning the thresholds and rendering a still to check.
studio.installed: Run `npx kinetograph plugins` to see that a plugin is installed; agents read its skill from there.

templates.title: Cyberpunk Reel
templates.description: A nine-second pop-art reel at 1920 by 1080: a person cut out of footage is painted in blue anime tones over a halftone background, with jagged rays, flying low-poly shapes, flames and a three-row title, and the cuts in and out break into shards and slices. You swap the footage and its matte, and the kicker and the two title lines.
change: The footage and its person matte (public/subject.mp4 and matte.mp4); the media tool crops the clip, makes the matte and tracks the person.
The title: the kicker and two title lines are props of the CyberpunkReel composition.

templates.title: Lyric Reel
templates.description: A seventeen-second square kinetic-type video in four looks: silver words stacking in a night sky full of glinting stars, black type on an orange band between letterbox bars, small blue words turning in the clouds, and a finale back in the stars. Words sit in 3D and one camera moves through them. You swap the words and the song.
change: The words, in words.ts: one entry per word with the frame it starts to arrive, the same count per shot or the layouts in shots/ adjusted.
The song, at public/song.mp3; it plays from 16.04 seconds in.

templates.title: Scrapline
templates.description: A hand-drawn border round a cut-out subject: a wobbly marker, pencil, crayon, scribble or brush line, on a sheet of torn paper behind it, both redrawn a few times a second like hand animation. You swap the subject and its matte, and choose the line style, the paper and the colour.
change: The subject: a video with a black and white matte, a video with alpha, an image with alpha, or an SVG path.
The style (Marker, Pencil, Crayon, Scribble, Brush), the paper (White, Kraft, Binder, Cardboard, your own picture or none), the line colour, the gap to the subject and the seed.

templates.title: Wish Reel
templates.description: An eighteen-second pop-art edit at 1440 by 1080: street footage flattens into pastel colours under ribbons of colour with 3D props tracked into it, then a helix of strands in a white void, a collage of photos in stop motion, black title cards and a typewriter ending. You swap the clips, whose cameras a bundled tool solves, or run the WishFilter composition on one video of your own.
change: The five clips and the camera track for each, made with the camera-tracking tool.
Or one video of your own, prepared as "input" with the prepare tool, for the WishFilter composition; it also takes eight photos for the collage.

templates.title: Word Flash
templates.description: A black-and-white type spot at 1080 by 1920 and 9.4 seconds, cut on every hit of its track: one word or a two-word lockup per cut, the background swapping black and white, ending with a last word that types on and blurs away. You swap the words, the track and the typeface.
change: The words, in script.ts (intro, run and outro). The run is one word per cut, so the word count has to match the number of cuts.
The track, at public/audio.m4a; a small tool finds its strongest hits and gives the cuts to paste into script.ts.
The typeface, FONT in lib.tsx. Positions are ink boxes, so another face lands in the same places.
